To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GMM-MMI, VQ and GLDS-SVM classifiers perform best in the context of mobile audio context recognition and, more importantly, the choice of the classifier is highly dependent on the application scenario.

(1) MFCCs are a good parametrization of mobile audio data for context recognition; (2) GMM-MMI performs the best among the GMM classifiers, but VQ performs better overall; and (3) the best accuracy of 52.01 % can be obtained with 3-second data segments using the VQ classifier.
GMM-MMI classifier performs the best with 3-second data segments and that the best classifier varies with different context, speaker and mobile device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of recognizing the context of a speaker from his or her utterances, using short audio segments and the speaker and language recognition (SLR) paradigm.
the problem of context identification from mobile audio data.
the problem of context recognition in mobile environments from short audio records.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best performing classifier is highly dependent on the context and user.
the performance of the classifiers is dependent on the context.
there is no single best classifier for all scenarios, but rather the choice of classifier is dependent on the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of the classifier should be made on the basis of the application requirements and the data characteristics.
the choice of classifier should depend on the type of context to be classified.
GMM-MMI is the best classifier for the task of context recognition, but it is not necessarily the best for each context or user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of classifier is less important compared to the choice of features and the amount of training data.
, in order to achieve high context identification rates in variable mobile environments, one needs to use a combination of multiple classifiers.

the context recognition performance is highly dependent on the type of classifier used, the type of feature used, the amount of training data, the amount of data used for recognition, the type of audio context, and, most important, the amount of background noise present in the data.
